0|f50de2d3811081957156b5d736778799379c29de|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"vmscan: have kswapd sleep for a short interval and double check it should be asleep
After kswapd balances all zones in a pgdat
column2: it goes to sleep.  In the

column1: event of no IO congestion
column2: kswapd can go to sleep very shortly after the

column1: high watermark was reached.  If there are a constant stream of allocations
from parallel processes
column2: it can mean that kswapd went to sleep too quickly

column1: and the high watermark is not being maintained for sufficient length time.
This patch makes kswapd go to sleep as a two-stage process.  It first
tries to sleep for HZ/10.  If it is woken up by another process or the
high watermark is no longer met
column2: it's considered a premature sleep and

column1: kswapd continues work.  Otherwise it goes fully to sleep.
This adds more counters to distinguish between fast and slow breaches of
watermarks.  A ""fast"" premature sleep is one where the low watermark was
hit in a very short time after kswapd going to sleep.  A ""slow"" premature
sleep indicates that the high watermark was breached after a very short
interval.
